questions.question: The <canvas> element is a:

options.text: Scriptable bitmap drawing surface (pixels drawn via JS)

questions.explanation: Canvas is a blank bitmap you paint on imperatively with the 2D (or WebGL) context — pixel-based, not DOM-based.

questions.question: To draw on canvas you first get:
questions.explanation: getContext('2d') returns the drawing API (fillRect, moveTo, etc.). For 3D you'd request 'webgl'.

questions.question: ctx.fillRect(10, 20, 100, 50) draws a rectangle at:
questions.explanation: fillRect(x, y, w, h): top-left corner at (x,y), then width/height. Origin is top-left, y grows downward.

questions.question: Canvas differs from SVG in that it is:

options.text: Immediate-mode raster (no retained object model; redraw to change)

questions.explanation: SVG keeps addressable DOM nodes; canvas paints pixels and forgets them — you must redraw to animate/update.

questions.question: On high-DPI (Retina) screens, the common fix is:

options.text: Scale canvas.width/height by devicePixelRatio and ctx.scale(ratio, ratio)

questions.explanation: Without ratio scaling, canvas bitmaps look blurry on retina. Multiply backing store by DPR, scale the context, keep CSS size constant.

questions.question: When animating, you should clear the previous frame with:
questions.explanation: clearRect wipes the bitmap each frame so old drawings don't smear; then redraw the new state.

questions.question: ctx.beginPath(), moveTo(), lineTo(), stroke() draws:
questions.explanation: beginPath starts a new path; moveTo/lineTo define points; stroke() renders the outline (fill() would paint it).

questions.question: Chart.js and similar libraries render via:
questions.explanation: Most 2D charting libs paint to canvas for performance with many data points; some offer an SVG renderer too.
